book.author: Howard Marks

callout.text: The smartest guys in the room

storyboard.claim: The smartest guys on Wall Street built massively leveraged portfolios on complex Gaussian copula models.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The consensus investor at his trading desk with price monitors, smirking confidently, holding a sheet of model notes to his chest.

beats.narration: Their models looked at decades of historical data and assumed that nationwide home prices could never decline all at once across the entire country.

storyboard.claim: Their models assumed from decades of data that nationwide home prices could never decline all at once.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A causal chain: a clock station labelled DECADES OF HISTORICAL DATA draws in, then a check station HOME PRICES COULD NEVER DECLINE; the later stations wait as dashed '?'.
storyboard.onScreenText: Decades of historical data / Home prices could never decline
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the confident trader to the chain of reasoning behind his models.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the assumption as the first link of a causal chain whose end is still unknown.

causal.action: looked at decades of historical data and assumed
causal.after: home prices assumed never to decline
causal.quote: assumed that nationwide home prices could never decline

beats.narration: Right. They equated historical price stability with future safety. Exactly. They looked at their neat historical models and relied on normal outcomes prevailing.

storyboard.claim: They equated historical price stability with future safety and relied on normal outcomes.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The same chain; a check token tagged FUTURE SAFETY is born on the 'never decline' station.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Keeps the chain and adds the token: the false sense of safety drawn from the past.
storyboard.addedInformation: Makes the leap from 'stable before' to 'safe ahead' a visible carried object.

causal.action: equated historical price stability with future safety
causal.quote: They equated historical price stability with future safety

beats.narration: They literally engineered their portfolios. assuing a nationwide housing crash, a true black swan outlier, was a statistical which is wild in hindsight.

storyboard.claim: They engineered their portfolios assuming a nationwide housing crash was a statistical impossibility.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The same chain; a lock station ENGINEERED THEIR PORTFOLIOS draws in and the FUTURE SAFETY token travels into it.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Adds the third station: the safety belief is built into the portfolios.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the belief becoming a concrete design decision.
storyboard.directorNote: kind decision, but the narration adds a step to the causal chain and the beat is staged as that chain -> kind mechanism

beats.narration: And because they thought risk was gone, they leveraged up 30 to1. So when reality broke their models, they were utterly decimated.

storyboard.claim: Because they thought risk was gone they leveraged up 30 to 1, and when reality broke their models they were decimated.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The same chain completes: a coin station LEVERAGED UP 30 TO 1, then a cross station UTTERLY DECIMATED; the token reaches the end.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Adds the last two stations: leverage and the wipe-out.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the end of the chain: the false safety led straight to ruin.

causal.quote: they leveraged up 30 to1. So when reality broke their models, they were utterly decimated

beats.narration: They confused the map for the territory. Joel Greenblat actually chimes in on this exact point in the text, pointing out that many academic versions of risk completely miss the practical reality

storyboard.claim: They confused the map for the territory; Greenblatt says academic versions of risk miss the practical reality of investing.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A two-bucket sorter: ACADEMIC RISK on one side, PRACTICAL REALITY on the other.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the collapse to the lesson: the model (map) is not the market (territory).
storyboard.addedInformation: Splits the two notions of risk the next example will contrast.

causal.quote: many academic versions of risk completely miss the practical reality

storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the two notions of risk to a concrete example.

storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the academic reasoning as a built claim, ready to be rejected.
